about: Which gene every file of Rouh belongs to (rouh/genes/owners.py, GENES.md "Every file belongs to a gene"). A new file goes under the gene it is part of; a new gene only for a new ability.

outside.workspace/**: The person's own work: tasks, steps and their files. Not Rouh's code.

foundation.name: Foundation
foundation.what: Rouh's frame: the Django project, its database and migrations, its settings and clock, and the rules every change follows.

turn-loop.name: Conversation turns
turn-loop.what: One turn of Rouh's: the message read, the model asked, its tools run and the answer streamed back, in a chat, by voice or on the phone.

screen.name: The screen and its cards
screen.what: What Rouh shows: the page with its conversation, canvas and orb, every card it draws and the pages it opens on the canvas.

model-calls.name: Model calls
model-calls.what: The LLM service: the one way any part of Rouh asks a model, whichever company's, at the model and level the Models page sets.

llm-request-log.name: LLM request log
llm-request-log.what: Rouh keeps a full log of every request made of a model, with its cost, reasoning, settings and metadata.

landing.name: Landing and deploying
landing.what: How a change reaches the live Rouh: land.sh replays it onto main with its checks, pushes it and deploys both services.

encrypted-offsite-backup.name: Encrypted offsite backup
encrypted-offsite-backup.what: Rouh's copies of itself: on a server, the nightly dumps sent weekly to Cloudflare R2, encrypted with gpg (deploy/backup_offsite.py); in a stack, a database copy every night by the backup part and, weekly, the whole Rouh as one bundle encrypted in age's format, sent to R2 or any S3 by the core, eight kept, and checked.

gene-registry.name: Genes and their history
gene-registry.what: The list of Rouh's genes, the file that says which gene every part of Rouh belongs to, every change written into a gene's history, and the switches.

run-program.name: Run program
run-program.what: Rouh holds and runs sessions of Claude Code, logs every tool call, and lets a person take a run over from a terminal and hand it back.

test-worlds.name: Test worlds
test-worlds.what: Throwaway Rouhs with stand-ins for every outside service, where each change is proved in a real browser before it lands.

chat-kinds.name: Chat kinds
chat-kinds.what: Rouh treats General and every other chat as two kinds, each with its own trimming rules and default model, and each chat can be set to Cheap, Smart or Auto beside the composer.

conversation-forks.name: Conversation forks
conversation-forks.what: Lets a chat be forked into a side conversation that stays linked to its source, with its own table, never shown in the chat lists.

memory-recall.name: Automatic memory recall
memory-recall.what: Before Rouh answers, a small model reads what the message is about, and the people, tasks and topics it names are looked up in Synapse.

events.recalled: You sent Rouh a message, and it answered with what Synapse knew about what you named

google-calendar.name: Google Calendar
google-calendar.what: Rouh reads and writes every calendar the connected Google account can see, from a conversation.

mail-alerts.name: Mail alerts
mail-alerts.what: Watches Gmail via Pub/Sub push and sends a Telegram note when a new message is judged worth attention.

worker-outbox.name: Worker outbox
worker-outbox.what: A background job queues an email it wants sent to the person, and Rouh sends it from the outbox table.

job-gateway.name: Rouh's tools for background jobs
job-gateway.what: Every background job uses Rouh's own tools through one gateway, run by Rouh with its own logins and ruled on in code by one permission check: reads run within the job's scope, what is risky becomes one decision, and what no tool gives is asked with request_from_rouh and logged. Files out of mail are two of its tools.

object-addressing.name: Object addressing
object-addressing.what: Every chat, run, task, project and artifact in Rouh has its own URL so it can be bookmarked, shared or reopened directly

self-link-resolution.name: Self-link resolution
self-link-resolution.what: Rouh recognizes links to its own pages and reads them directly as the signed-in person instead of fetching them over the web.

public-page-sharing.name: Public page sharing
public-page-sharing.what: Lets a page from the workspace be made public at a token address anybody can open without signing in.

ask-ai-page-editing.name: Ask AI page editing
ask-ai-page-editing.what: Rouh lets you point at part of a shared or public page and ask AI to edit it directly, with undo, and lets guests sign up by email to view shared pages.

page-comments.name: Page comments
page-comments.what: Rouh lets people on a shared page leave Figma-style pinned comments with tags, resolving and orphan snapshots, and Rouh and its agents read, add, change and take away those comments with the page_comments tool.

page-highlights.name: Page highlights
page-highlights.what: Rouh lets a reader highlight passages of text on an HTML page in chosen colours, kept per reader and page.

page-definitions.name: Page definitions
page-definitions.what: Rouh lets a reader select a term or passage on an HTML page and press Define beside Ask, which explains it in a tooltip in the light of the page and leaves it underlined, so hovering it later shows the same explanation.

page-history-and-options.name: Page history and options
page-history-and-options.what: Rouh keeps a history of every change to a page, who made it and when, and lets a version be kept as a switchable option over the page.

x-ray-report-layer.name: X-ray report layer
x-ray-report-layer.what: Adds an X-ray layer over long research reports showing a one-sentence answer, an argument map, a numbered claim outline and a doubts tab, without changing the report.

your-part.name: Your part
your-part.what: The hands-on things only the person can do, which hold up work Rouh is doing: told apart from decisions, each with its own page (what to do, the steps with their links, how Rouh checks it, the story so far), answered with Done, Not doing this or Another way, asked about in place, and withdrawn by itself when the work no longer needs it.

event-log.name: Event log
event-log.what: Rouh records every action done in it and by it to an append-only, partitioned event log, with a first view under Settings, Stats.

voice.name: Talking and listening
voice.what: Rouh's ears and mouth: the microphone heard, the end of a turn told from the words, and every answer spoken aloud.

orb-sound-feedback.name: Orb sound feedback
orb-sound-feedback.what: Plays distinct musical notes for jobs, helpers and tool calls while the orb is open, with quiet ambient music underneath.

falling-stars-decoration.name: Falling stars decoration
falling-stars-decoration.what: Rouh shows an occasional falling star animation across the navigation sidebar for decoration.

image-generation.name: Image generation
image-generation.what: Rouh generates and edits pictures through a provider-neutral imaging interface, currently backed by OpenAI's image API.

linkedin-research.name: LinkedIn research
linkedin-research.what: Rouh searches LinkedIn by name, shows a card of candidate people to pick from, then harvests the chosen profile.

meeting-guest-research.name: Meeting guest research
meeting-guest-research.what: Rouh looks up every guest at an upcoming external meeting on LinkedIn ahead of time and saves what it finds to their Synapse contact.

events.guests_shown: You asked Rouh who is coming to a meeting, and saw its guests

meeting-contacts.name: Meeting guests into contacts
meeting-contacts.what: Rouh adds every guest of the owner's meetings of fewer than twenty people to their iCloud contacts, leaving out family, rooms, lists, bots and anybody already there.

events.added_contact_shown: You looked at a contact Rouh added from one of your meetings

runs.added: Rouh added the guests of your meetings to your iCloud contacts

feedback-triage-board.name: Feedback triage board
feedback-triage-board.what: Reads feedback, writes feature requests, starts runs for them and tracks each through to Done on the board.

nightly-refactoring.name: Nightly refactoring
nightly-refactoring.what: Every night at 03:00, after the feature run, up to ten refactors of Rouh's code side by side, each with Undo in the morning brief.

n11-asked-again.name: Asked again
n11-asked-again.what: A request you keep typing by hand on different days is offered, once, as scheduled work that Rouh does for you at the time you usually ask.

events.offered_again: You asked again for something you asked for before, and Rouh offered to do it regularly

n13-plain-words.name: Plain words
n13-plain-words.what: A term you would not know is explained in plain words where Rouh or a run first uses it, and a term you ask the meaning of is explained every time after.

events.term_kept: You asked what a term means, and Rouh kept it to explain every time

n14-n14-copies-in-step.name: Copies kept in step
n14-n14-copies-in-step.what: When you ask for a change to work that exists in two forms, such as a deck's HTML slides and its Google Slides copy, the run changes both, and says so.

events.copies_named: You started a run in a task whose work has copies, and it was told to change them all

n15-n15-short-answers.name: Short answers
n15-n15-short-answers.what: When you ask Ask AI what a word or a passage means, or say "shortly", you get a few plain sentences instead of a page.

events.kept_short: You asked Ask AI a short question, and got a short answer

n16-facts-told-on-a-page.name: Facts told on a page
n16-facts-told-on-a-page.what: A fact you tell Ask AI about your work in passing is kept in the task's notes, so every later run, chat and page in that task knows it without your saying it again.

events.fact_kept: You told Ask AI a fact on a page, and Rouh kept it

n17-sent-by-you.name: Sent by you
n17-sent-by-you.what: When you send a reply yourself, from your own mail, to email a task drafted for you, Rouh finds it in your sent mail and keeps it in the task's notes in your own words, so the task knows it went and what you said.

events.reply_kept: You sent, from your own mail, a reply a task had drafted for you, and Rouh kept it in the task

night-3.name: Before you meet
night-3.what: Before a meeting with people from outside, the morning brief's opened meeting and a Telegram an hour before say who is coming and the last emails with each.

events.meeting_opened: You opened a meeting in the morning brief and saw who is coming from outside

night-5.name: What to raise
night-5.what: Before a meeting with people from outside, one read of the mail with them says where things stand, what to raise and why, and what is open.

events.corrected: You corrected What to raise for a meeting

runs.read: Rouh read the mail with a meeting's guests and said what to raise

night-6.name: After the meeting
night-6.what: After each recorded meeting, the work it calls for is offered in Decisions, with why, its task and when; Start begins a run briefed with the meeting.

events.work_started: You pressed Start on work a meeting called for

runs.work_offered: Rouh offered work a meeting called for in Decisions

night-7.name: What to raise remembers
night-7.what: What to raise also reads the earlier meetings with the same people, and keeps every correction you make for every later meeting with them.

events.correction_kept: You corrected What to raise, and Rouh kept it for later meetings with them

runs.remembered: What to raise used earlier meetings, or what you told it before

n18-newest-first.name: Newest in the thread first
n18-newest-first.what: A reply in a thread never goes out over a newer message in it: when somebody wrote again after the message being answered, the reply waits and the newer message is read first; on a draft card it is shown, and Send again sends it as it is.

events.held_back: A reply was about to go over a newer message in its thread, and waited until the newer message was read

n18-since-read.name: Since you last read it
n18-since-read.what: When a page you open on the canvas has changed since you last saw it, the bar over it shows What changed, and pressing it has Ask AI say what changed: each visit keeps the page's words, and nothing is asked of a model before the press.

events.pressed: You pressed What changed on a page that had changed since you last saw it

runs.offered: A page you opened had changed since you last saw it, so What changed was on its bar

n19-mail-pictures.name: Pictures in mail seen
n19-mail-pictures.what: A picture or a scan with no words, attached to an email, is shown to Rouh as itself when it opens the file, so it can say what the screenshot, the photo or the scanned page shows instead of saying it cannot see pictures.

events.seen: Rouh opened a picture or a scan attached to an email, and saw it as itself

n20-follow-through.name: Followed through
n20-follow-through.what: When a job Rouh started finishes, Rouh is reminded of the step it told the person it would do once the job was done, and does it, and checks the job's report against everything added to the job while it ran, asking the job for what it left out.

events.kept_word: A job you asked for finished, and Rouh was handed the step it told you it would do once the job was done
events.added_checked: A job finished, and Rouh checked its report against what you added to it while it ran

n20-doc-changes.name: What changed in a doc
n20-doc-changes.what: Asked what changed in a Google Doc since a day, Rouh reads the document's saved versions in Drive and says who changed it, each paragraph added, taken out or changed, and the comments made since.

events.read: You asked what changed in a Google Doc, and Rouh read its saved versions and comments

n21-copy-exact.name: Copy kept word for word
n21-copy-exact.what: Copy given to Ask AI for a page, line by line or with the copy to stay as written, is checked on the page word for word after Ask AI changes it; Ask AI is told what is not there as given and puts it right, and what is still not right is named under its answer.

events.checked: You gave Ask AI copy for a page, and what landed on the page was checked word for word
events.corrected: Copy you gave Ask AI was not on the page as given, and Ask AI was told to put it right

n22-doc-comments.name: Comments read with the doc
n22-doc-comments.what: Whatever reads a Google Doc through read_doc, a chat, a job or Ask AI, is given the doc's open comments after its text: who wrote each, the words it is on, what it says and the answers so far.

events.read: You had Rouh read a Google Doc with comments on it, and it read the comments with the text

n22-askai-docs.name: The Google Doc you link
n22-askai-docs.what: A Google Doc, Sheet or Slides deck linked in a question to Ask AI is read before it answers and given to it with the question, so copy can be linked instead of pasted; for an invited guest only a document the task's own notes link.

events.read: You linked a Google Doc in a question to Ask AI, and it read the document before answering

n22-doc-reply.name: Answer a comment
n22-doc-reply.what: Asked to answer a comment in a Google Doc, Rouh writes the answer under it from its own Google account, in the words given, and marks it resolved when asked.

events.answered: You asked Rouh to answer a comment in a Google Doc, and it wrote the answer under it

base-patches.name: Patch-level base updates
base-patches.what: What every Rouh runs on, kept patched without touching its code: a base image with no Rouh code, Rouh's code in a volume of its own, a nightly look for patch-level fixes, and each Rouh's own checks and the security checks before it switches.

protected-core.name: The protected core
protected-core.what: rouh-guard: the safety and repair parts a Rouh uses and cannot edit - the key proxy, the base check with the frozen security checks, the start scripts, the signature check on a shared gene, the change step with its undo points, and the doctor - and the Rouh's two small sides of it, the check face and the guard's client; and the owner's timed grants the key proxy reads (GitHub, and servers past its lists), with git and gh in the worker that use them.

n23-doc-last-changed.name: Who last changed it
n23-doc-last-changed.what: A Google Doc, Sheet or Slides deck Rouh reads through read_doc, in a chat, a job or Ask AI, comes with when it was last changed, on your clock, and who changed it.

events.read: You had Rouh read a Google document, and it was told when it was last changed and by whom

n23-doc-comment.name: Leave a comment
n23-doc-comment.what: Asked to comment on a Google Doc, Rouh writes a new comment in it from its own Google account, in the words given, on the passage named, which is checked against the document first.

events.commented: You asked Rouh to comment on a Google Doc, and it wrote the comment in it

n24-askai-follow.name: Follow-ups stay where you were
n24-askai-follow.what: After Ask AI changes a page, its next turn is told which part of the page that change was in, by the heading above it and its words, so words like "it" or "great, but" are read as being about that part, and its answer names the part it changed.

events.followed: You asked Ask AI more after it changed a page, and it was told where its last change was

n24-task-rename.name: Rename a task
n24-task-rename.what: Asked in words to rename a task or a step, Rouh renames it: its row, its folder's .object.json and, for a step, the title its task's meta gives it; the folder and every link stay as they are.

events.renamed: You asked Rouh to rename a task or a step, and it did

n25-askai-words.name: Where your words are
n25-askai-words.what: Words quoted in a question to Ask AI are found on the page before it answers: how many places they are in, under which heading and in which part of the page, and a phrase cut short with ".." is matched to the heading nearest it; when they are in more than one place, Ask AI asks which before it changes anything.

events.located: You quoted words of a page to Ask AI, and it was told where on the page they are

n25-step-move.name: Move a step
n25-step-move.what: Asked in words to move a step, Rouh moves it into another task, out as a task of its own, or out as the first step of a new task, renumbered as Move in its three dots does, with its old number kept for search.

events.moved: You asked Rouh to move a step, and it did

n25-share-remind.name: Remind them
n25-share-remind.what: In the Share panel, beside a person shared with by hand who has not opened it a day after the invitation, Remind them opens a new email to them in Gmail, in your own mailbox, with the page's name and their link.

events.reminded: You pressed Remind them beside a person in the Share panel who had not opened what you shared

n26-each-point.name: Every point accounted for
n26-each-point.what: A job asked to apply comments, feedback or a review, or given three or more numbered changes, is told to find every point first, go through them one at a time, check each against the result, and end its report with one line per point: Done, Partly or Not done, and why.

events.told: You asked for several comments or changes to be applied, and the job was told to account for each one

n26-comments-by.name: Their comments
n26-comments-by.what: Asked in words, Rouh finds every comment and answer one person left on the Google Docs, Sheets and Slides decks linked in the tasks' notes and changed lately in Drive: the document, the task, the words it is on, what it says, when, whether it is open or answered, and a link to it.

events.found: You asked Rouh for somebody's comments, and it looked through the documents for them

moving-in.name: Moving a Rouh in
moving-in.what: An existing Rouh, on a server or in another stack, exported as one bundle (its database, its encryption and Django keys, its data directory and workspace) and brought into a fresh stack before its first start, every saved login still opening.

n27-deck-slides.name: Decks read slide by slide
n27-deck-slides.what: Whatever reads a Google Slides deck through read_doc, a chat, a job or Ask AI, is given it slide by slide: each slide by its number, with its title, its words, its speaker notes and the open comments on it, and the link that opens any one slide.

events.read: You had Rouh read a Google Slides deck, and it read it slide by slide with its speaker notes and comments

n27-find-slides.name: Find a slide
n27-find-slides.what: Asked in words, Rouh finds the slides themselves in the person's Google Slides decks, by their words and speaker notes, each with its deck, its number and a link that opens the deck on it.

events.found: You asked Rouh to find a slide, and it looked through your decks slide by slide

n28-doc-pictures.name: Pictures in docs seen
n28-doc-pictures.what: The pictures in a Google Doc Rouh reads, a diagram, a screenshot or a photo, are marked where they stand in its words and shown to Rouh as themselves after them, so it can say what they show instead of reading round them.

events.seen: You had Rouh read a Google Doc with pictures in it, and it saw them as themselves

n28-page-asks.name: What they asked on your pages
n28-page-asks.what: Asked in words, Rouh lists what each person asked Ask AI to do on your pages: when, who, on which page, their request in their own words, what Ask AI did and whether it was undone, with a count by person and by page.

events.listed: You asked Rouh what somebody asked Ask AI to change on your pages, and it listed their requests

n29-sheet-tabs.name: Sheets read tab by tab
n29-sheet-tabs.what: A Google Sheet Rouh reads is read with every tab by its name, in the sheet's order, each with its rows numbered and its columns lettered, as the sheet shows them, instead of only its first tab as comma-separated text.

events.read: You had Rouh read a Google Sheet, and it read every tab of it

n29-sheet-write.name: Written into a sheet
n29-sheet-write.what: Asked in words, Rouh writes cells or adds rows in a Google Sheet, as if typed, and says what every changed cell held before.

events.written: You asked Rouh to put something in a Google Sheet, and it wrote it

n30-doc-suggestions.name: Suggested edits read as suggestions
n30-doc-suggestions.what: In a Google Doc Rouh reads, each suggested edit nobody has accepted yet is marked where it stands, a suggested insertion or a suggested deletion, and counted under the title, instead of being read as if it were already the document's words.

events.read: You had Rouh read a Google Doc with suggested edits in it, and it told them apart from the words

n30-slide-write.name: Written into a deck
n30-slide-write.what: Asked in words, Rouh replaces words on a Google Slides deck's slides and writes their speaker notes, and says what each held before.

events.written: You asked Rouh to change words or speaker notes in a Google Slides deck, and it wrote them

n31-drive-files.name: Files in Drive read
n31-drive-files.what: A PDF, Word, Excel or PowerPoint file kept in Google Drive is read like a document when Rouh is asked about it, instead of being refused as a file with no words.

events.read: You had Rouh read a PDF, Word, Excel or PowerPoint file in your Drive, and it read its words

n31-drive-copy.name: A copy made when asked
n31-drive-copy.what: Asked in words, Rouh makes Drive's own copy of a document, sheet, deck or any file, names it, files it in the folder asked for and fills in the words asked for, leaving the original as it was.

events.copied: You asked Rouh to copy a file in your Drive, and it made the copy

n32-inside-files.name: Files inside files read
n32-inside-files.what: A forwarded email (.eml) and a zip archive, attached to an email or uploaded, are read like any document: the email's sender, date, subject and words, and every document inside either one, instead of being refused or read as raw code.

events.read: You had Rouh read a forwarded email or a zip archive an email brought, and it read what was inside

n32-calendar-away.name: Away and focus time
n32-calendar-away.what: Asked in words, Rouh puts Google Calendar's own out-of-office or focus-time block on your calendar, which declines meeting invitations in that time by itself with your message, instead of an ordinary event that declines nothing.

events.blocked: You asked Rouh to mark you out of office or keep focus time, and it put Google's own block on your calendar

n33-mail-invites.name: Invitations read on your clock
n33-mail-invites.what: When Rouh reads an email carrying a meeting invitation, it reads the invitation's calendar file too: what it is (new, changed, cancelled, an answer), when on your own clock with the sender's time beside it, how long, where, the call link, who sent it and who is invited.

events.read: You had Rouh read an email carrying a meeting invitation, and it read the invitation's time on your clock

n33-when-free.name: When others are free
n33-when-free.what: Asked in words, Rouh reads colleagues' free and busy times from Google, with your own, and says the times when everybody can meet, and whose calendar Google would not show.

events.asked: You asked Rouh when other people are free, and it read their free and busy times

n33-busy-guard.name: Not booked over someone busy
n33-busy-guard.what: Before Rouh books or moves a meeting with guests, it reads their free and busy times; if one of them is busy then, nothing is booked or emailed, and Rouh says who is busy and the next times when everybody is free.

events.held: You asked Rouh to book or move a meeting into a time a guest is busy, and it held it and offered times when everybody is free

n34-away-replies.name: Away, said their automatic reply
n34-away-replies.what: Before Rouh drafts or sends an email, or books a meeting with guests, it looks in your mailboxes for an automatic reply from each of them in the last three weeks that says they are away, and says when they are back and whom it names instead.

events.told: You had Rouh write to or book somebody whose automatic reply says they are away, and it told you first

n34-not-arrived.name: Did not arrive
n34-not-arrived.what: An email Rouh sent for you that bounced is told to you at once in a notice: to whom, which email, and why it did not arrive, with Open the chat it was sent from.

events.opened: You pressed Open on a notice that an email Rouh sent did not arrive

runs.told: Rouh told you in a notice that an email it sent did not arrive

n34-to-answer.name: Waiting on your answer
n34-to-answer.what: Asked in words, Rouh reads your inboxes for the emails from people that you have not answered, each with what they asked, who, when and how long it has waited.

events.asked: You asked Rouh which emails you have not answered

n34-inbox-unsubscribe.name: Unsubscribe in the inbox card
n34-inbox-unsubscribe.what: A newsletter or a shop's mail opened on the inbox card has an Unsubscribe button: one press stops it (RFC 8058 one-click), or opens the sender's own page.

events.unsubscribed: You pressed Unsubscribe on a newsletter opened on the inbox card

files.name: One home for every file
files.what: Every file Rouh is handed lives once, in the folder of the task, chat or project it belongs to, on one list of files, at a path Rouh and every job see read and write.

n33b-meet-link.name: Booked with a call link
n33b-meet-link.what: When Rouh books a meeting with guests and no place, it gives it a Google Meet link, the way the Add Google Meet button does, and says so; told there should be no link, it adds none.

events.booked: You had Rouh book a meeting with guests and no place, and it went out with a Google Meet link

n33b-calendar-link.name: A calendar link read
n33b-calendar-link.what: Given the link of a calendar somebody published (an .ics or webcal address), Rouh reads it whole and says what is on it day by day on your clock, with weekly repeats, dates taken out and moved meetings worked out.

events.read: You gave Rouh a calendar's link, and it read what is on it on your clock

n33b-address-check.name: A mistyped address caught
n33b-address-check.what: Before Rouh sends an email, each address is compared with the ones you already have; one that is a letter or two off a known address (dana@northwnd.com for dana@northwind.com, gmial.com) is not sent, and Rouh asks whether you meant the known one.

events.held: You asked Rouh to email an address a letter or two off one you know, and it held the email and asked which you meant

n34b-attach-promised.name: A file promised, not attached
n34b-attach-promised.what: Before Rouh sends an email whose words say a file is attached (attached, enclosed, прикачен, приложено) and that carries no file, it is not sent; Rouh finds the file the email means and attaches it, or asks. A draft that says so is made, with a line saying the file is not on it yet.

events.held: You had Rouh write an email that said a file was attached, and Rouh held it, or said so on the draft, because no file was on it

n34b-public-holidays.name: Public holidays read from Google
n34b-public-holidays.what: Asked whether a day is a holiday in a country, or which holidays a country has in a span, Rouh reads Google's own public holiday calendar for it instead of answering from memory.

events.asked: You asked Rouh about the public holidays in a country, and it read them from Google's holiday calendar

n34b-inbox-remind.name: Remind me about this email
n34b-inbox-remind.what: A message opened on the inbox card has Remind me: This evening, Tomorrow morning or Monday morning; one press makes a reminder on Clockwork that brings the email back to you then, with what it asks of you.

events.reminded: You pressed Remind me on an email opened on the inbox card

n35-their-clock.name: On their clock too
n35-their-clock.what: Before Rouh sends or drafts an email that names a time, to somebody whose own mail is written on another clock, it is told the hour on their clock, so the email says both.

events.told: You had Rouh write a time to somebody on another clock, and it said the time on theirs too

n35-renewal-notice.name: Renews soon
n35-renewal-notice.what: An email saying a subscription renews or a free trial ends and charges is told to you at once in a notice: what, when, in how many days and how much, with Open the email.

events.opened: You pressed Open the email on a notice that a subscription renews soon

runs.told: Rouh told you in a notice that a subscription renews or a trial ends soon

n35-unread-lists.name: Newsletters you never open
n35-unread-lists.what: Asked in words, the newsletters and lists in your mailboxes whose mail of the last two months you never opened, each with how many came, and stopped in one word.

events.asked: You asked which newsletters you never open
events.stopped: You had Rouh unsubscribe from lists you never open

n35-their-hours.name: Not in their night
n35-their-hours.what: Before Rouh books a meeting with a guest abroad, it reads the guest's clock from their own newest email, and a meeting that falls before 08:00 or ends after 20:00 for them is not booked until you have heard their hour and the hours inside both days.

events.held: You had Rouh book a meeting that fell in a guest's early morning or night, and it said their hour before any invitation went

n36-holiday-guard.name: Not booked on a guest's public holiday
n36-holiday-guard.what: Before Rouh books a meeting with a guest whose address is in another country's domain, it reads Google's public holiday calendar for that country, and a meeting on a day off there is not booked until you have heard whose holiday it is.

events.held: You had Rouh book a meeting on a day that is a public holiday in a guest's country, and it said so before any invitation went

n36-meeting-hours.name: Where your meeting time went, by company
n36-meeting-hours.what: Asked how much time went into meetings, or with whom, Rouh counts your main calendar exactly over the span, by company and by person, your own company apart, each against the span before.

events.asked: You asked Rouh how much of your time went into meetings, or with a company or a person, and it counted your calendar

n36-meeting-soon.name: You meet them soon
n36-meeting-soon.what: An email opened on the inbox card from somebody you meet in the next seven days, or with them on it, says when and which meeting, with Open the meeting.

events.opened: You pressed Open the meeting on an email from somebody you meet soon, on the inbox card

runs.shown: Rouh said on an email you opened that you meet somebody on it in the next days

n36-their-language.name: In their language
n36-their-language.what: Before Rouh sends or drafts an email, it reads the language each person it goes to writes to you in, from their own newest email, and an email in another language waits until it is written in theirs or you say it is fine.

events.told: You had Rouh write to somebody in another language than the one they write to you in, and it was told theirs before the email went

n36-promised-to-you.name: Promised to you by mail
n36-promised-to-you.what: Asked in words, Rouh reads your inboxes for what people promised you by email by a day: which days have passed with nothing from them since, which are coming, and which may have come.

events.asked: You asked Rouh what people promised you by email, or what you are still waiting for

n36-promise-watch.name: If it does not come
n36-promise-watch.what: An email opened on the inbox card that promises you something by a day has If it has not come by that day, tell me: one press, and Rouh looks for it the morning after and tells you only if nothing came.

events.watched: You pressed If it has not come, tell me on an email opened on the inbox card

design-standard.name: The design standard
design-standard.what: Everything a person sees is designed one way, in two tiers chosen by the agent: journeys first, one direction, Anthropic's guide read privately at run time, a check of the screens at 1440 and 390 px, critic rounds on the full tier, and a landing that refuses a change to the screen without a clean record.

n37-got-it.name: Got it on Telegram
n37-got-it.what: Every message you write to Rouh on Telegram is marked 👀 the moment Rouh takes it, before any answer starts, so you see at a glance it arrived.

events.marked: You wrote to Rouh on Telegram and it marked your message 👀 as taken

n37-reply-times.name: Reply times with a company
n37-reply-times.what: Asked how quickly you and a company (or a person) answer each other's email, Rouh counts the conversations in your mailboxes: the usual time each side takes, your slowest answers, and what is still waiting on either side.

events.asked: You asked Rouh how quickly you and a company answer each other's email, and it counted your mailboxes

n37-waiting-too.name: Also waiting on you
n37-waiting-too.what: An email opened on the inbox card names the sender's other conversations whose last word is still theirs, with Open, so answering one does not leave the other waiting.

events.opened: You pressed Open on another email of the sender's still waiting on you, on the inbox card

runs.shown: Rouh said on an email you opened that its sender has other emails waiting on you

n37-their-questions.name: Their other questions
n37-their-questions.what: Before Rouh sends or drafts an email in your turn, it reads whether anybody it goes to asked you something else in another email that is still unanswered, and the email waits once so it can answer that too, or say it will be answered apart.

events.held: You had Rouh send an email to somebody with another question to you still unanswered, and it was held once to answer it too
events.told: You had Rouh draft an email to somebody with another question to you still unanswered, and it was told before you read the draft

n37-between-us.name: Between you and them
n37-between-us.what: Asked in words about one person, Rouh reads your inboxes for what is open between you by email, both ways: what they asked you that you have not answered, what you promised them, what they promised you, and when each of you last wrote.

events.asked: You asked Rouh where things stand with somebody, or what is open between you and them by email

n37-answer-watch.name: If I have not answered it, remind me
n37-answer-watch.what: An email opened on the inbox card from a person that asks you something has If I have not answered by tomorrow, remind me: one press, and Rouh looks the next working morning and reminds you only if you have not answered.

events.watched: You pressed If I have not answered by tomorrow, remind me on an email opened on the inbox card

n38-not-twice.name: Not put on twice
n38-not-twice.what: Before Rouh books an event, it looks at your calendars around that time: when the same meeting is already there (the same title, or every guest already on it), nothing is booked and nobody gets a second invitation, and Rouh says where it already is.

events.held: You asked Rouh to book something already on your calendar, and it said where it is instead of booking it twice

n38-away-after.name: Away, after Rouh wrote
n38-away-after.what: When somebody Rouh emailed for you answers with an out-of-office reply, you are told at once: who is away, until when in their own words, whom they name for anything urgent, with Open the chat it was sent from.

events.opened: You pressed Open on a notice that somebody Rouh wrote to is away

runs.told: An out-of-office reply to Rouh's email came, and you were told in a notice

n38-no-company.name: Contacts with no company
n38-no-company.what: Asked which contacts have no company, Rouh reads every contact in your iCloud address book and lists those whose Company is empty, each with what it should most likely say: from a colleague's contact at the same company, guessed from a work address, or who they are to you.

events.asked: You asked Rouh which of your contacts have no company, and it read all of them

n38-know-them.name: How you know them
n38-know-them.what: An email opened on the inbox card from somebody you have not written with for months says when you last wrote and about what, when you first wrote and who introduced you, with Open the last and Open the first.

events.opened: You pressed Open the last or Open the first on an email from somebody back after months, on the inbox card

runs.shown: Rouh said on an email you opened when you last and first wrote with its sender

n39-sent-twice.name: Not sent twice
n39-sent-twice.what: Before Rouh sends an email, it reads its own Sent mail of the last day: when the same email already went to the same people, with the same subject and words, nothing is sent again and Rouh says when it went.

events.held: You asked Rouh to send an email that had already gone, and it said when it went instead of sending it twice

n39-new-number.name: A new number in their signature
n39-new-number.what: When a contact's email reaches Rouh with a phone number in its signature that their contact does not have, you are told at once, with Add it to their contact, which puts the number on the contact in iCloud.

events.added: You pressed Add it to their contact on a notice of a new number in somebody's signature

runs.told: A contact's email had a number in its signature their contact lacks, and you were told in a notice

n39-same-contact.name: Contacts kept twice
n39-same-contact.what: Asked which contacts are there twice, Rouh reads every contact in your iCloud address book and groups the cards that are one person (the same address, the same number or the same name), with what each card has and which to keep.

events.asked: You asked Rouh which of your contacts are there twice, and it read all of them

n39-save-sender.name: Save them as a contact
n39-save-sender.what: An email opened on the inbox card from somebody who is not in your contacts says so, with what would be saved (name, address, company, the numbers in their signature) and Save to contacts, which adds them to iCloud in one press.

events.saved: You pressed Save to contacts on an email from somebody who was not in your contacts, on the inbox card

runs.shown: Rouh said on an email you opened that its sender is not in your contacts

n40-draft-twice.name: Not drafted twice
n40-draft-twice.what: Before Rouh writes a draft, it reads its own Drafts: when the same draft (same people, subject and words) is already there, no second one is made and Rouh gives the one that is there.

events.held: You asked Rouh to draft an email that was already in its Drafts, and it gave you that draft instead of making a second one

n40-new-address.name: A new address for a contact
n40-new-address.what: When somebody in your contacts writes from an address that is on none of their cards, you are told at once, with Add it to their contact, which puts the address on the contact in iCloud.

events.added: You pressed Add it to their contact on a notice that a contact wrote from a new address

runs.told: A contact wrote from an address not on their card, and you were told in a notice

n40-contact-card.name: Their card to pass on
n40-contact-card.what: Asked to pass somebody's contact on, Rouh makes their card file (.vcf) with the name, company, numbers and addresses only, leaving out your notes, the birthday and the photo, ready to attach to an email.

events.made: You asked Rouh to pass a contact on, and it made their card file to attach

n40-card-in-mail.name: A contact card in an email
n40-card-in-mail.what: An email opened on the inbox card that carries a contact card says whose it is and what it holds, with Save to contacts, or Add to their contact when the person is in your contacts already.

events.saved: You pressed Save to contacts or Add to their contact on an email carrying a contact card, on the inbox card

runs.shown: Rouh said on an email you opened whose contact card it carries

n41-forward-twice.name: Not forwarded twice
n41-forward-twice.what: Before Rouh forwards an email or a whole conversation, it reads the Sent mail of the last day: when the same email already went to the same people, it is not forwarded again and Rouh says when it went.

events.held: You asked Rouh to forward an email it had already forwarded to the same people, and it told you when instead of sending it again

n41-new-company.name: A new company in their signature
n41-new-company.what: When somebody in your contacts signs an email with a company their contact does not say, you are told at once, with Change it on their contact, which writes the new company to the contact in iCloud.

events.changed: You pressed Change it on their contact on a notice that a contact signs with a new company

runs.told: A contact signed an email with a company their card does not say, and you were told in a notice

n41-contact-changes.name: What changed on a contact
n41-contact-changes.what: Asked what changed on a contact, Rouh reads the earlier versions it keeps of the card and says each change and when, newest first, and on your yes puts the contact back as it was before one of them.

events.read: You asked Rouh what changed on a contact, and it listed the changes and when
events.put_back: You said yes to putting a contact back as it was, and Rouh wrote it to iCloud

n41-call-sender.name: Call them from their email
n41-call-sender.what: An email opened on the inbox card from somebody whose number Rouh has shows Call and their numbers, mobile first, each one press away from ringing.

events.called: You pressed a number on an email's Call line on the inbox card
